title: Introduction to Spreadsheets
source: ICT Grade 3 (Nile International) Block 2 Week 3 Study sheet pp.19-33

scenes.t: A worksheet, also called a spreadsheet, is made of cells where you can enter and calculate data. The cells are organized in columns and rows.
To open Microsoft Excel: go to the Start menu, write Excel in the search, and click the Excel icon.
Columns go down, and they are named with letters: A, B, C. Rows go across, and they are numbered: 1, 2, 3.
A cell is where a column and a row meet. Every cell has an address: the column letter first, then the row number. Examples: A7, B5, C10.
The formula bar shows what is inside the active cell. The active cell is the cell that is selected right now.
A cell range is a group of selected cells. For example, A1 to A5, or A1 to C5.
The fill handle is a small square in the bottom right corner of a cell. You can drag it to copy what is inside.
To rename a worksheet, right click on it, choose Rename, and write the new name. To add a new worksheet, click the plus button.
To save your work: choose the File tab, choose Save as, choose Browse, pick a place like Desktop, and press Save.
In Excel there are three data types: text, numbers and formulas.
